extDesc.message: Removes the paywall and article limit on the New York Times website. Free and open source.

articleHeadline.message: You Have 3 Minutes of Unlimited Access.

step1Desc.message: Find the extension icon in your browser toolbar.

step2Desc.message: Click to open the New York Times Unlocker menu.

step3Desc.message: Ensure the protection switch is set to Active.

bodyP1.message: We have granted you 3 minutes of free, unlimited access to test the power of New York Times Unlocker. Browse any article, anywhere on The New York Times, with zero interruptions.

bodyP2.message: After your trial ends, you will have a daily limit of 10 free articles. To continue reading without limits, simply upgrade to our lifetime plan.

feat1Desc.message: No more paywalls blocking your view. Articles unlock automatically as you browse.

feat2Desc.message: Your reading habits remain yours. We do not track your history or sell your data.

noteBody1.message: An earlier version of this extension removed the New York Times paywall, then added one of its own: three minutes of unrestricted use, then a cap of ten articles a day, then a payment to lift the cap.

noteBody2.message: That version was published under the Mozilla Public License, whose section 3.2 requires that source code be made available to anyone who receives the software. It was not. This version removes the cap, removes the payment, and publishes the source the licence always required.

nowLine.message: There is no timer. There is no daily limit. There is nothing to buy.

ev1What.message: A call to a remote server on every install

ev1Detail.message: It sent a generated device ID, your platform and your full user agent, and returned the flag that decided whether you had to pay.

ev2What.message: A request to Google on every popup open

ev2Detail.message: Both extension pages loaded remote webfonts. This version uses fonts already on your computer and makes no network requests of its own.

ev3Detail.message: Including a 78 KB component bundle that was loaded on every popup and never called once.

footerLicence.message: Free software under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.

statusSignedInSub.message: You have a New York Times session — standing down.

statusDisabledSub.message: The paywall is not being blocked.

ev4What.message: A daily limit nobody kept track of

ev4Detail.message: In 49 of its 54 languages the extension promised two free articles a day. Its code allowed ten. The translations had not been re-read in a long time.
